subject: Invoice trigger and Exhibit G: temporary onboarding credit + redlines
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@cloudmed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudMed Procurement <procurement@cloudmed.com>, Victor Li <vli@cloudmed.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed tweak to invoice trigger + onboarding credit (Order Form DL-9082)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Procurement asked us to put two items on paper before we move to signature: 1) change the invoice trigger so CloudMed is invoiced only after Acceptance is confirmed (rather than at provisioning), and 2) a temporary onboarding credit to offset overages for the first 90 days while models are tuned.

I attached a short redline of the Order Form and a draft Exhibit G (acceptance criteria) — see attachments. Can you confirm if Redwood is able to accept the invoice-trigger wording (we appreciate this is a billing/finance ask) and whether a 90‑day credit is feasible from your side (we're thinking 15% of estimated monthly spend applied as a credit, to be reconciled at month 3).

Happy to hop on a quick call Thursday AM if that helps.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Procurement
CloudMed Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@cloudmed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed tweak to invoice trigger + onboarding credit (Order Form DL-9082)

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the redlines. Quick replies below and looping in Karthik (AM) and Laura (legal) for the specifics.

- Invoice trigger: We typically invoice on provisioning to keep billing predictable, but we understand why CloudMed prefers Acceptance-based invoicing for the onboarding window. That's potentially doable as a short-term carveout for Exhibit G, provided we limit it to initial onboarding (e.g., first 60–90 days) and keep a defined acceptance confirmation process.

- Onboarding credit: Conceptually okay; we need to confirm the math and the accounting treatment. Karthik — can you model 15% credit versus a fixed $ credit? Finance will want a reconciliation approach in the SOW.

Laura — can you weigh in on acceptance wording and the legal risk if we move the invoice trigger? Specifically: any concerns about cashflow or precedent if we accept Acceptance-based invoicing for CloudMed only?

If everyone is aligned, we'll produce a clean Order Form with a short Exhibit G clause and a one‑page mutual action plan for signature. We can also gate DocuSign so the invoice trigger clause is visible to procurement and finance for sign-off.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@cloudmed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed tweak to invoice trigger + onboarding credit (Order Form DL-9082)

Alicia / Jordan —

I ran a quick model. Two options look reasonable from a commercial perspective:

1) Percentage credit: 15% credit to be applied against invoices for months 1–3, with a true-up at the end of month 3. If usage is materially higher (>25% vs estimate) we convert the credit to a one-time invoice adjustment (to avoid undercharging).

2) Fixed credit: $30k onboarding credit applied as a one-time invoice line in month 1; reconciled at month 3 with usage report.

Pros/cons: percentage credit scales with CloudMed's usage (preferred from customer-experience POV). Fixed credit is simpler for Finance. Either way we should capture the reconciliation method and a cap.

I can produce the updated Order Form with both options as alternatives (strike/insert) so legal can pick. Laura — if you prefer one approach, say so and I'll build it into the redline.

I'll also flag: if we switch invoice trigger to Acceptance for onboarding, Finance wants a signed acceptance checklist (Exhibit G) before the first invoice posts. Sample language below: "Invoices for months 1–N shall be held pending executed Acceptance; Redwood will provision resources but will not issue invoices until (i) Customer confirms Acceptance via Exhibit G checklist and (ii) any onboarding credits are applied."

Karthik
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@cloudmed.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed tweak to invoice trigger + onboarding credit (Order Form DL-9082)

Alicia / team —

Thanks for the proposals. High-level legal guidance:

- Acceptance-based invoice trigger: acceptable as a limited carveout for onboarding provided the clause has (a) clear acceptance criteria (Exhibit G), (b) a maximum onboarding period (60–90 days) and (c) a fallback if Acceptance is delayed beyond X days (e.g., invoices auto-run at day 90 unless Customer provides written notice). This avoids indefinite hold on billing.

- Credit mechanics: we prefer fixed credit (cleaner audit trail). If the customer insists on a percentage credit, include a hard cap and explicit reconciliation steps. Add language that credits are applied against future invoices and do not convert to refunds.

- DocuSign flow: recommend a separate DocuSign envelope for the onboarding Exhibit G to ensure Finance and Legal can validate Acceptance before invoices run. Also propose a short mutual action plan attachment (1 page) enumerating sign-off responsibilities.

I've attached inline markup suggestions and a proposed fallback sentence for delayed Acceptance. If you want, I can generate a final redline of the Order Form with the fixed-credit option and the Exhibit G language for signature.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: laura_exhibit_g_comments.docx (docx)]

Subject: Re: Proposed tweak to invoice trigger + onboarding credit (Order Form DL-9082)

Jordan / team —

Quick note to confirm CloudMed prefers the percentage credit (15% for months 1–3) but we agree to a cap of $40k and the reconciliation at month 3. We also accept the fallback you proposed: if Acceptance is delayed beyond 90 days, invoices will post automatically and credits will be adjusted.

Please proceed with the redline using the percentage credit with a $40k cap and include the Exhibit G checklist and DocuSign flow. Will aim to review the redline within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Victor Li
VP, Platform Ops
CloudMed Health

[Note: CloudMed will route final sign-off through legal; expect a short turnaround after redline is received.]
